articles.title: UP Politics: Election Heat Rises Over Caste, Religion and Vote Banks
articles.description: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election, political rhetoric has intensified, with the BJP and opposition parties exchanging allegations over caste, religion and voter blocs. At a BJP event in Meerut, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath attacked his political opponents while invoking issues such as Lord Ram, the Kanwar Yatra and Sanatan traditions. BJP president Nitin Nabin also highlighted religious and cultural issues during his visit. The report links this messaging to the BJP’s focus on its Hindu voter base. The report cites CSDS-Lokniti data showing that in 2017, the BJP received around 47% of Hindu votes and 5% of Muslim votes, while the SP received 19% of Hindu votes and 46% of Muslim votes. In 2022, the BJP’s figures were 54% among Hindu voters and 8% among Muslim voters, while the SP received 26% and 79%, respectively. Meanwhile, AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi is seeking an alliance in Uttar Pradesh and has set October 2 as a deadline for announcing his alliance plans. The Samajwadi Party has indicated that it intends to continue with its existing alliance arrangement. The report notes that AIMIM has not yet won a seat in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. According to the cited voting-pattern data, the SP received 79% of Muslim votes in 2022, compared with 6% for the BSP, 3% for Congress and 8% for the BJP. The competing parties are therefore focusing heavily on Hindu and Muslim voter blocs as the 2027 election approaches.

articles.title: Dalit Battle: BJP, SP & BSP Step Up Outreach Ahead of 2027
articles.description: Uttar Pradesh’s political focus is increasingly turning toward the Dalit electorate ahead of the 2027 Assembly election. The report highlights the importance of Dalit voters and the efforts of the BJP, Samajwadi Party and BSP to strengthen their support among the community. The Samajwadi Party is promoting its PDA strategy, with the “D” representing Dalits, and has raised the issue of alleged attacks on statues of Dr B.R. Ambedkar. Akhilesh Yadav has also focused on reserved constituencies and has spoken about protecting the Constitution. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, opposition parties won nine of Uttar Pradesh’s 17 SC-reserved seats, while the BJP won eight. The SP won seven, Congress one and Chandrashekhar Azad’s ASP(KR) one. The BJP, meanwhile, is seeking to maintain its support among Dalit voters through its outreach and welfare initiatives. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has also attacked previous SP governments over issues concerning Dalit icons and institutions. BSP chief Mayawati has separately sought to retain her party’s traditional Dalit support, accusing rival parties of turning to Dalit symbols only during elections. The 2024 Lok Sabha results also saw the BSP win no seat in Uttar Pradesh, while the SP won 37 and BJP 33 overall. Overall, the report focuses on how the BJP, SP and BSP are positioning themselves around Dalit representation, Ambedkar’s legacy and reserved constituencies ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.
